A cruise line management game with real ports and real limits

Cruise Line Architect is a deep cruise-line management sim. Every port has a real berth length and channel depth, so the biggest ships don't fit everywhere and a river boat never leaves the river. Each departure has its own booking curve, and a ship that sails half-empty stays half-empty.

The money works the way the industry does: ticket revenue plus onboard spending, against fuel, crew, food, port taxes and travel-agent commission. Plan a long voyage badly and the fresh food runs out at sea.

The world map

204 real ports in 11 regions

The Caribbean, the Mediterranean, Alaska, the Danube, Northern Europe, New England, South America, Australia and the Pacific, the Far East, expedition-only Antarctica, and the 60-to-140-night world cruise. Each region has its own seasons.

Itineraries

See the profit before she sails

Choose where guests board and where they leave, the ports of call, the nights and the fare. A live forecast answers every change with occupancy, revenue, costs and profit per sailing before you commit.

Sea lanes

Draw your own route

Draw the sea lane yourself. The course you draw sets the fuel bill, so a detour around a headland costs real money on every sailing.

Resupply

Stock her for the long haul

Plan where each ship loads fresh food, frozen and dry stores, and fuel. Buy at the pier or sign vendor contracts, and price every bunkering stop. An Antarctic expedition that runs out of fresh food costs you goodwill on every sailing.

Your fleet

Keep every ship in shape

Order new from the yard, hunt the used market or charter. Hulls wear: send a tired ship for a drydock refresh or a full revitalization, and keep her five-year class survey current, or she can't sail.

Run every part of the line

Every port has a story

Tap any port for a short introduction, its berth and depth limits, and every route you run through it.

Sail around the world

Run world cruises of 60 to 140 nights, with open-jaw voyages that start and end in different ports.

Weather is a decision

Hurricanes, mechanical failures and port closures arrive as choices, and the clock waits while you decide.

A cruise industry that moves around you

Fill every cabin

Cabins sell through the weeks before each departure, faster in the January-to-March wave season.

23 rival lines

Twenty-three real rival lines redeploy their fleets by region and season and chase the same guests. Your reputation decides how hard they bite.

Six ship classes

From a 190-guest Danube longship and an ice-class polar explorer to a 5,600-berth megaship.

The long game

Run launch campaigns and borrow against your fleet. With Pro, buy out a rival line or list your company once it's worth $500 million. Miss your payments and the lenders close in.

Made for iPhone and iPad

Cruise Line Architect is built natively for iPhone and iPad. On iPad the map gets the whole screen beside a sidebar. Speed time up to 25× and watch the fleet cross the oceans.

A single one-time purchase, Cruise Line Architect Pro, unlocks a third ship and beyond, buying out rival lines and taking your company public.

Cruise Line Architect FAQ

Is Cruise Line Architect free?

Yes. It's free to download and play with a fleet of up to two ships, with every region and system. A one-time purchase, Cruise Line Architect Pro, unlocks a third ship and beyond, buying out rival lines and going public. There's no subscription and there are no ads.

Are the ports real?

Yes. The game has 204 real ports in 11 cruising regions, each with a real berth length and channel depth, so not every ship fits every port.

Can I design my own cruise itineraries?

Yes. You choose where guests board and leave, the ports of call, the nights and the fare, and you draw the sea lane yourself. A live forecast shows the profit per sailing before you commit.

What kinds of ships can I run?

Six classes, from a 190-guest Danube river longship and an ice-class polar explorer to a 5,600-berth megaship. Order new from the yard, buy used or charter.

Is Cruise Line Architect on Android or PC?

Not at the moment. It's made for iPhone and iPad and requires iOS or iPadOS 18 or later.

Do I need an internet connection?

No. Your cruise line runs on your device. A connection is used for Game Center and the one-time purchase.

Can I play the same game on iPhone and iPad?

Saves stay on the device you play on, with three save slots. The Pro purchase restores on any iPhone or iPad signed in to the same Apple Account.

Is it like Airline Architect?

It's from the same studio and shares the business side: loans, going public and buying rivals. The cruise game adds its own systems: booking curves, berth and depth limits, open-jaw voyages, drawn sea lanes, resupply and class surveys.
